title: Restriction of scalars along a square of ring objects
statement:
Let $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a lax monoidal functor between monoidal categories, and
let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
R_Y & \xrightarrow{\ \varphi_Y\ } & S_Y\\
{\scriptstyle\eta_R}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle\eta_S}\\
FR_X & \xrightarrow{\ F\varphi_X\ } & FS_X
\end{array}
$$

be a commutative square of morphisms of monoid objects, with $\varphi_X\colon R_X\to S_X$ in
$\mathcal C$ and $R_Y,S_Y$ monoid objects of $\mathcal D$. With $\mathrm{mapMod}(F)$ the
transport of module objects of [sk-def-sfb-transport] and $\operatorname{Res}$ the restriction of
scalars of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], the natural isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi_Y}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_S}\circ\mathrm{mapMod}(F)
\;\cong\;
\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_R}\circ\mathrm{mapMod}(F)\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi_X}
\colon\Mod_{S_X}(\mathcal C)\longrightarrow\Mod_{R_Y}(\mathcal D)
$$

is the one under which both sides are $\mathrm{mapMod}(F)$ followed by the restriction of
scalars along the common composite $\eta_S\circ\varphi_Y=F\varphi_X\circ\eta_R$.

proof.text: Write $\mu^F_{A,B}:FA\otimes FB\to F(A\otimes B)$ for the lax structure map. Let $M$ be an $S_X$-module with action $\gamma:S_X\otimes M\to M$. By [def-sfb-modobj-transport] and [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], the left composite has underlying object $FM$ and action $a_L=F(\gamma)\circ\mu^F_{S_X,M}\circ(\eta_S\otimes 1_{FM})\circ(\varphi_Y\otimes 1_{FM})=F(\gamma)\circ\mu^F_{S_X,M}\circ((\eta_S\circ\varphi_Y)\otimes 1_{FM})$. The equality is functoriality of tensoring with $FM$. Thus it is transport followed by restriction along $\eta_S\circ\varphi_Y$.

source.place: the single proof paragraph, expanded on module actions

proof.text: The same definitions give the right composite the underlying object $FM$ and action $a_R=F(\gamma\circ(\varphi_X\otimes 1_M))\circ\mu^F_{R_X,M}\circ(\eta_R\otimes 1_{FM})$. Functoriality of $F$ and naturality of its lax structure in the first variable give $F(\varphi_X\otimes 1_M)\circ\mu^F_{R_X,M}=\mu^F_{S_X,M}\circ(F\varphi_X\otimes 1_{FM})$. Hence $a_R=F(\gamma)\circ\mu^F_{S_X,M}\circ((F\varphi_X\circ\eta_R)\otimes 1_{FM})$. The assumed square says $F\varphi_X\circ\eta_R=\eta_S\circ\varphi_Y$, so $a_R=a_L$. This also identifies the right composite with restriction along that same common composite.

source.place: the single proof paragraph, expanded on module actions

proof.text: For each $M$, take $1_{FM}$ in both directions between the two resulting $R_Y$-module objects. By [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], clause 2, the module-linearity equation is $1_{FM}\circ a_L=a_R\circ(1_{R_Y}\otimes1_{FM})$, which follows from $a_L=a_R$ and the identity laws. The two composites are identities. Both composite functors send a module morphism $h:M\to N$ to $Fh$ on underlying morphisms by [def-sfb-modobj-transport] and [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]; naturality of the chosen components is therefore $Fh\circ1_{FM}=1_{FN}\circ Fh$. This defines the asserted natural isomorphism, whose identifications with transport followed by restriction along the common composite are precisely the identity identifications of steps 1 and 2.
